newsitem.title: UK: BA up on American alliance hopes.
newsitem.headline: BA up on American alliance hopes.

text.p: Shares in airline British Airways Plc rose in early trade on Monday, helped by a report the British government is poised to approve BA's proposed alliance with American Airlines.
BA shares touched 590p in early dealings but slipped slightly to trade at 589p by 0800 GMT, up 5-1/2p on the day. Over 514,000 shares had changed hands. The broader market was slightly lower.
The Sunday Times newspaper, citing "airline and Whitehall (government) sources", said UK Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang was expected to approve the deal later this month.
The report said that under the terms of the approval, BA will surrender a number of take-off and landing lots at Heathrow airport to reduce its share of the transatlantic market.
It added that BA may have to share Heathrow's Terminal Four, which it dominates, with other carriers.
Analysts said the terms outlined in the report, if accurate, were consistent with expectations and were unlikely to prompt changes to BA share recommendations.
"There are no real showstoppers. The bigger hurdles are across the Atlantic with U.S. regulatory clearance and anti-trust," Paribas Capital Markets analyst Chris Avery said.
Avery said most people expected the Office of Fair Trading to clear the proposed alliance.
"The OFT has become yesterday's story," he said.
Stephen Clapham, analyst at Robert Fleming, sounded a cautious note on BA's recent share performance.
"I think we have to put it in context. BA's share was 550p when the American deal was announced and it hasn't done that much relative to the market since," he said.
